newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Icy weather kills stranded Ukrainian zoo animals.
newsitem.headline: Icy weather kills stranded Ukrainian zoo animals.

text.p: Two jaguars, a pheasant and a monkey have frozen to death in Ukraine after a touring zoo got stuck in the foothills of the Carpathian mountains and other animals could face the same fate.
"A jaguar couple has just died because of heavy frosts and a lack of food. A pheasant and a monkey have died too," circus director Rayisa Didenko told Reuters by telephone on Friday.
"We have given the animals all the heaters we have and taken the other monkey to live with us," she added.
A few visitors have been coming to see the animals and some locals had even brought food, but it was not enough, she said.
The zoo of 20 animals, including lions, bears and donkeys, had been heading for the Ukrainian city of Uzhgorod near the Hungarian and Slovak borders.
But it stopped at the western town of Ivano-Frankivsk in November and heavy snow falls and black ice in the treacherous mountain roads have kept it there ever since, Didenko said.
The zoo, usually based in the western city of Rivne, spends twice as much keeping the animals as it earns from charging one hryvnia (60 cents) per child and two hryvnias ($1.20) per adult.
"We have also been paying 250 hryvnias (about $140) per month to the local authorities to rent this so-called plot of land, which is in fact just waste ground," Didenko said.
She added that the zoo would continue its tour when the weather got warmer.
